description: SSOT for the machine-checkable half of the superdesign anti-slop gate. `references/anti-slop.md` used to claim this role and did not hold it: the detectors were hardcoded greps inside anti-slop-gate.sh, so a rule change was a two-place edit and drifted. The prose file keeps the catalog, the reasoning and the judge-only lens; the machine rules live here and anti-slop-gate.sh reads them.

layers.src: decidable by reading source text — anti-slop-gate.sh
layers.dom: needs a rendered page — design-audit.mjs (no rule carries this layer yet)

engines.grep: ERE over the comment-stripped file set
engines.grep-raw: ERE over the raw file set; the comment IS the defect
engines.perl: perl regex per line, for \x{} codepoint ranges BSD grep cannot express
engines.absent: fires when the pattern appears NOWHERE in the target
engines.offscale: grep, then keep only px values outside `scale`
engines.count-threshold: grep, then fire only at >= `threshold` matches
engines.purple-oklch: grep, minus the DESIGN.md-declared and chart-validated exemptions
engines.state-coverage: select files by `selectPattern`, fail those missing any of `requireAll`

rules.label: indigo/violet/purple default accent
rules.failureMode: The reflexive accent. An indigo/violet/purple utility or hex is the single most common thing a model reaches for when no brand hue was decided, so its presence says the colour was never chosen. Fix: pick the accent in Phase 1 and express it as an OKLCH token.
rules.source: references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors (Starter Pack, hex tell-list)

rules.label: Tailwind purple/violet/indigo laundered through an OKLCH token
rules.failureMode: The same reflexive purple, converted to OKLCH so no hex or utility grep can see it — shadcn's own dark --chart-4 IS Tailwind purple-500. Window L 0.40-0.79, C >= 0.15, hue 270-319. The 270 floor is measured, not guessed: blue-700 sits at hue 264.376 and indigo-500, the first genuinely indigo step, at 277.117, so a 250 floor flagged every blue brand as purple. Two exemptions or the rule punishes every legitimately violet brand: (a) a custom property NAMED in DESIGN.md is the project's declared brand hue; (b) a --chart-N slot in a stylesheet whose palette already passes validate-chart-palette.mjs, because a computed check outranks a hue heuristic.
rules.source: references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors + Tailwind v4 palette, measured 2026-07-27

rules.label: unedited shadcn default chart/destructive palette (= Tailwind palette in OKLCH)
rules.failureMode: Class D: byte-identical to a published substrate default. It asserts nothing was decided here — a human who ran `shadcn init` and shipped trips it identically, and that is the correct verdict. Fix: derive the chart ramp from the brand hue and re-run validate-chart-palette.mjs.
rules.source: shadcn/ui default globals.css; references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors § SUBSTRATE-DEFAULTS

rules.label: colored left-border strip
rules.failureMode: The card/nav tell: a coloured 2-4px left strip is the default way a model signals category or state without designing a hierarchy. Fix: carry the distinction with weight, gray level or spacing.

rules.label: brand hue as active/selected fill
rules.failureMode: Selection is a UI state, not a brand moment. Filling the selected row with the brand hue spends the accent's 10% budget on chrome and leaves nothing to point at what matters. Fix: a neutral accent surface plus a weight change.

rules.label: banned default display font
rules.failureMode: Inter/Roboto/Open Sans/Lato as the display face is the typographic centre of the training distribution — no personality, and no evidence a face was chosen. Fix: name the archetype's face as a positive replacement (BANNED x -> USE y); a ban with no replacement leaves the probability mass nowhere to go.
rules.source: references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors § TYPOGRAPHY + Starter Pack

rules.label: off-scale spacing (outside the declared ramp)
rules.failureMode: Class S: an arbitrary px value outside the project's own declared ramp. The ramp is enumerated, not `n % 4`: modulo passes 20/28/36/40/44 — every value the ramp deliberately omits — and would false-flag the two Fluent Nudge half-steps (6, 10). Fix: snap to the nearest ramp step or add the step to the ramp deliberately.
rules.source: references/tokens.md § the declared ramp; Fluent 2 Nudge steps

rules.label: flat uniform 0.1 black shadow reused
rules.failureMode: One flat black shadow at exactly 0.1 opacity, reused everywhere, is elevation with no role in it — every surface floats the same amount, so depth carries no information. Fires only at 4+ occurrences: a single use is a choice, a fourth is a default. Fix: a role-based scale (raised / overlay / popover), tinted toward the surface hue.
rules.source: references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors § DEPTH/SHADOW + Starter Pack

rules.label: leading emoji in heading
rules.failureMode: A leading emoji in an H1-H6 is one of the strongest 'a chat model wrote this' tells and does the job an icon component should do, with no size, colour or a11y control. Fix: an icon element, or nothing.

rules.label: Tailwind v3 syntax in a v4 project (stale-weights leak)
rules.failureMode: v3 syntax inside a v4 project is not a style choice, it is the model emitting weights that predate the framework the project actually uses — and half of it silently does nothing. Bare `ring` must be a whole utility inside a class attribute, or the rule eats the word 'ring' in prose and the `ring` half of v4's own `ring-ring` colour utility. Fix: the v4 spelling (tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide).

rules.label: banned output marker (lazy stub / self-narration)
rules.pattern: //[[:space:]]*(\.\.\.|rest of( the)? code|implement here|TODO|similar to above|continue pattern|add more as needed)|/\*[[:space:]]*\.\.\.[[:space:]]*\*/|for brevity|the rest follows the same pattern|similarly for the remaining|and so on|I.ll leave that as an exercise
rules.failureMode: A stub marker means the file was never finished and the gap was narrated instead of filled. Read from the RAW file, not the comment-stripped scan — the comment IS the defect here.

rules.label: self-narrating comment in shipped code
rules.failureMode: Chat narration left in the artifact: the comment explains the assistant's next step rather than the code's reason. Read from the RAW file for the same reason as AS-09.

rules.label: outline-none with no focus-visible replacement
rules.failureMode: In Tailwind v4 `outline-none` also kills the forced-colors outline, so a keyboard user in high-contrast mode loses the focus indicator entirely. Only a defect when nothing restores a visible one: shadcn's own primitives pair `outline-none` with `focus-visible:ring-[3px]` on the same class string, which is correct, and flagging the bare token made every vetted primitive a tell and taught the reader to ignore the detector.

rules.label: round element < 34px — a violation only if it is a target (SC 2.5.8 inscribed square)
rules.failureMode: A round target needs d >= 34px for its inscribed square to reach 24x24. NOTE, never a hard tell: grep sees geometry and never interactivity. A `size-4 rounded-full` may be a switch thumb (pointer-events-none, not a target at all) or a decorative dot, and `h-5 w-9 rounded-full` is a pill track whose inscribed square is not its height. Those two shapes are excluded outright; what survives still needs a human to confirm the element is a target.

rules.label: placeholder font never replaced
rules.failureMode: tokens.md / theme.css plant this marker precisely so the gate can catch a theme that was generated and never art-directed. Its presence means Phase 2 ran and Phase 1 did not.

rules.label: positive tabIndex
rules.failureMode: A positive tabIndex pulls the element out of DOM order and reorders focus for the whole document, so the keyboard path stops matching the visual one (SC 2.4.3). Fix: order the DOM, use 0 or -1.

rules.label: legacy combobox (aria-owns / role=combobox on a non-input)
rules.failureMode: The ARIA 1.0/1.1 combobox shape. Screen readers shipped support for the 1.2 pattern years ago and the old one now announces inconsistently across NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver. Fix: role=combobox on the input itself, aria-expanded + aria-controls.

rules.label: render-blocking @import of Google Fonts
rules.failureMode: A CSS @import of a font stylesheet serialises two round-trips before any text paints, which lands directly on LCP. Fix: <link rel=preconnect> + <link rel=stylesheet>, or self-host.

rules.label: transition-all
rules.failureMode: `transition-all` animates every property that ever changes, including layout properties nobody meant to animate, so it is both a motion tell and an INP cost. Fix: name the properties (transform, opacity, colors).

rules.label: img without width/height (CLS)
rules.failureMode: An with no intrinsic size reserves no box, so everything below it jumps when the image arrives — a direct CLS hit. `fill` is exempt because a Next.js fill image gets its box from the positioned parent.

rules.label: no prefers-reduced-motion reset
rules.failureMode: Fires when the WHOLE target contains no reduced-motion reset anywhere. Vestibular disorders are not an edge case and SC 2.3.3 is not optional; a build with motion and no reset has simply never considered the reader who cannot take it.

rules.label: generator deployment artifact left in the build
rules.pattern: lovable\.dev|Built with v0|Built on Lovable|\.replit\.dev|Crafted with love|Built with care
rules.failureMode: A deploy string from the generator that produced the page. Unlike palette-based attribution — which the state of the art cannot support (macro F1 0.345 on which-generator) — a literal deploy string is class D and takes seconds to check.
rules.source: arxiv.org/pdf/2604.26990v1 (generator attribution collapses); references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors

rules.label: data components missing loading/error/empty
rules.failureMode: A component that fetches has three states besides success, and shipping only the success state is the most common way a generated screen looks finished and is not. SELECTION IS THE WHOLE RULE (field-run F5): it used to select any file containing `.map(`, which is every static marketing section that maps over a literal array — those were then asked for loading/error/empty states they cannot have, making the detector unpassable on any marketing surface. The selector now requires an actual async or data-source signal; a `.map()` over a hardcoded array is not a data component.
rules.source: evals/field-runs/README.md F5; references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors § STATES, TOKENS & A11Y

rules.label: curly quotes/apostrophes in source strings (ChatGPT/DeepSeek tell)
rules.failureMode: Investigate, never fail. Curly quotes are a ChatGPT/DeepSeek default, but Chicago style, Word and macOS substitution produce them too — the human population behind this signal is far too large for it to block a ship. Class P: density only.
rules.source: references/anti-slop.md § Automatable detectors § 0 (class P: no single class-P tell may block a ship)
